findings.excerpt:
exact ⟨e, (ambientHyperplane_comap_equation _ v U i φ hφ).trans
    (congrArg (fun f => Ideal.span ({f} : Set Γ(X, U.1))) (he v).symm)⟩
findings.problem: The proof joins the two equations with `.trans` and `congrArg`. That needs an explicit lambda `fun f => Ideal.span ({f} : Set Γ(X, U.1))` with a type ascription, plus a `.symm`. The idea is simple: first use the ambient-hyperplane equation, then replace the polynomial expression with the section coefficient. The `congrArg`/`.trans`/`.symm` plumbing hides that idea, and the reader has to work out which side of which equation is being rewritten.
findings.proposed_change:
Rewrite with the two lemmas inside the anonymous constructor:
```lean
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := sectionsMorphism_affine_equation k s hs U i φ hφ
  exact ⟨e, by rw [ambientHyperplane_comap_equation _ v U i φ hφ, he v]⟩
```
After the first rewrite the left side becomes `Ideal.span {∑ j, φ (chartConstants i (v j)) * φ (chartCoordinate i j)}`. `he v` then turns the coefficient term `U.1.topIso.hom (coefficient e (restrictSection U.1.ι (sectionCombination k s v)))` on the right side into that same sum, and `rw` closes the goal by `rfl`.
findings.benefit: The proof becomes two named rewrites in the order of the argument: pull back the ambient hyperplane equation, then identify the coefficient with the chart polynomial. The hand-built `congrArg` motive with its `Set Γ(X, U.1)` ascription and the `.symm` are gone, so there is less bookkeeping to decode and the key idea is easier to see.
